SPSS Compatibility

Source: vignettes/spss-compatibility.Rmd
spss-compatibility.Rmd

The statistical functions of mariposa are checked against reference output of IBM SPSS Statistics 29. This article lists, for each function, how many SPSS values its tests compare and which results are not compared with SPSS.

mariposa 0.7.4, status of 2026-10-19.

Summary

  • 42 of 53 statistical functions are compared with SPSS output, with 14,622 SPSS values in total.
  • 2 documented algorithmic differences (see below).

How results are compared

Each comparison uses the precision with which SPSS prints the value:

  • Exact: counts, degrees of freedom, and p-values that SPSS prints as .000 (p < .001).
  • Printed precision: all other values agree with SPSS to within half a unit of the last decimal SPSS prints (one unit for p-values).
  • Documented difference: where SPSS and mariposa use different algorithms by design, the values agree within the tolerance listed under “Documented differences”.

The reference values come from SPSS syntax runs on the survey_data example data. The comparisons run with the package’s test suite on every change; the SPSS syntax and output are part of the source repository (tests/spss_reference).

Results by function

The w_*() functions share one set of SPSS references; each row shows that total. The last column lists results that are not compared with SPSS output. They are verified by other means: the weighted results of the rank-based tests reproduce the unweighted results exactly when all weights equal 1 (the weighted Mann-Whitney test also agrees with survey::svyranktest()), and the remaining results are checked against published formulas or independent implementations.

Documented differences

Function Results Tolerance Reason
efa() ML loadings, sums of squares, % of variance 0.002 SPSS stops the ML iteration at its convergence criterion (.001); mariposa iterates to the optimum.
efa() ML communalities / SS where SPSS did not converge 0.05 The SPSS reference runs end without convergence (3 factors from 6 items, df = 0, Heywood cases).

A documented difference describes a known difference between the algorithms, not an error; its tolerance is the agreement the two algorithms reach.

Functions without their own SPSS comparison

  • Computed by chi_square(), whose results are compared with SPSS: cramers_v(), goodman_gamma(), phi()
  • Data transformations, covered by unit tests: center(), pomps(), rec(), row_count(), row_means(), row_sums(), std()
  • Data documentation without an SPSS counterpart: codebook()
